in_sanskrit.name: अरिजा
in_sanskrit.long_meaning: The one who is the queen or consort of the God Indra. Indra is the Hindu God of the rain, thunder and lightning, and he is also the King of the Gods in Hindu mythology. Thus, Arija is the Goddess who is the Queen or consort of Indra.

in_hindi.name: अरिजा
in_hindi.long_meaning: The one who is dear to Indra. Indra is a Hindu God, and 'ari' means dear, and 'jana' means people. Thus, Arija is the one who is dear to the people of Indra.

in_tamil.name: அரிஜா
in_tamil.long_meaning: Arija is the consort of Indra, the Hindu God of rain, thunder and lightning. Indra is also known as the King of the Gods in Hindu mythology.

in_telugu.name: అరిజా
in_telugu.long_meaning: The Goddess of Indra. Indra is a Hindu God, and Arija is considered to be the Goddess of Indra.

in_marathi.name: Arija
in_marathi.long_meaning: Arija हे एक हिंदू नाव आहे जे भारतीय संस्कृतीत खोल आध्यात्मिक महत्त्व ठेवते। In Sanskrit, the name Arija comes from the Sanskrit word āri, meaning 'lord' or 'master'. The suffix -ja denotes a female. Thus, Arija can be translated as 'Lady' or 'Queen'. In Hindu mythology, Arija is also the name of a Yakshi, a female attendant of a deity. Yakshis are known for their beauty, grace, and compassion.
